statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of five representative public templates plus error handling; authentication, purchasing and personalized MY surfaces were not covered because they require account state and were not part of the unauthenticated core flow.

paths.description: Mobile landing page: discovery, ranking, navigation, global performance and security.
Weekday catalogue listing, representative of long browse/list templates.
Series landing and episode-list template; primary content selection journey.
Long-form comic reader, the primary content-consumption flow and highest layout-risk surface.
Search entry and genre navigation, representative form and discovery surface.
Unknown URL used to inspect HTTP/error handling.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture and the probe reports computed colorScheme "normal".
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens, with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.summary: Primary route/state changes use abrupt full navigations with no authored View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM and interaction inspection found conventional links and no authored view-transition CSS or startViewTransition calls on the representative navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for catalogue-to-series and series-to-reader navigation, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The landing page misses the modern loading-performance bar.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse scored performance 0.50 with LCP 19.1 s, FCP 2.7 s, TBT 540 ms and Speed Index 7.5 s; the independent trace measured LCP 3.27 s and TBT 80.8 ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP request chain, prioritize the hero/ranking imagery, and reduce/defer JavaScript before re-testing under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The episode reader shifts dramatically during load.
findings.evidence: The layout observer measured CLS 0.328 on the episode route from one large shift at about 1.33 s, well above the 0.1 good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic space for reader images and other late content using width/height or aspect-ratio, and keep insertion above existing content stable.

findings.summary: A large mostly-unused vendor bundle dominates the page load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,021 KiB unused JavaScript in the 1.43 MB vendor-common bundle (72.95% wasted); HAR records 1.58 MB of script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Split vendor code by route and feature, remove unused dependencies, and load optional advertising/analytics code conditionally after core content.

findings.summary: Secondary navigation and author text fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found #ccc on white at 1.6:1 and #999 on white at 2.84:1, below the required 4.5:1 for the observed text sizes.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace low-contrast gray tokens with colors meeting WCAG AA in every theme and verify all text states with automated and visual tests.

findings.summary: The document has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse landmark-one-main failed, and the DOM probe found HEADER and FOOTER but no MAIN landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the unique page content in a main element and retain the existing skip link target on or within it.

findings.summary: The viewport disables pinch zoom and several footer targets are too small.
findings.evidence: The viewport contains user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1; Lighthouse also found 9–15 px-high footer links below the 24 px target floor.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no/maximum-scale restrictions and expand small link hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The home page has no standard meta description.
findings.evidence: Both the DOM probe and Lighthouse meta-description audit found no meta[name=description], although an Open Graph description exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, page-specific meta name="description" and retain accurate Open Graph metadata.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes leave avoidable exposure.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no CSP or HSTS. XSRF-TOKEN and NACT lacked Secure, all four cookies used SameSite=None, and two identifiers last 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforced CSP and HSTS, mark HTTPS cookies Secure, use the strictest workable SameSite policy, and shorten identifier retention.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy coverage is incomplete and referrers are over-shared.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url; clickjacking and nosniff defenses were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Permissions-Policy and a privacy-preserving Referrer-Policy such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin; add frame-ancestors in CSP.

findings.summary: Most dynamic catalogue content is absent from the non-JavaScript representation.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 36% raw-to-rendered content coverage; the raw HTML had no H1, although it was not an empty JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful rankings/catalogue links and expose accurate structured metadata so non-JS agents can discover the same core content.

findings.summary: Image delivery is oversized, eager and legacy-format heavy.
findings.evidence: Images inspection found 38/38 legacy-format images, 31 oversized, 20 below-fold images without lazy loading and 8 without responsive sources; HAR transferred 1.84 MB of images.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes, right-size thumbnails, add dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold images while keeping the LCP image eager/high priority.

findings.summary: The landing page carries a large third-party/resource footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 75 requests and 3.53 MB transferred; 62 requests and 1.97 MB were classified third-party, including advertising and measurement origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route budgets, remove non-essential third-party requests, defer ads/measurement until after core content, and batch analytics events.

taskList.title: Cut LCP, unused JavaScript and request weight on catalogue routes
Restore zoom, target sizing, contrast and main landmark accessibility
Eliminate the episode reader’s large layout shift
Harden headers, cookie policy and referrer/privacy controls
Server-render core catalogue content and complete metadata
Add preference-driven dark theme and optional route transitions
